statements.text: The patient presents with fever and sore throat for three days, including a sore throat since Monday and no cough. Vital signs show a temperature of 38.4 °C and a heart rate of 96 bpm. The patient has a recorded moderate allergy to Penicillin with a rash reaction.
Fever and sore throat for three days.
Consider evaluating the duration of fever and sore throat in the context of the patient's age and lack of cough.
May be worth considering alternative antibiotics given the patient's history of Penicillin allergy.
Consider a throat swab to rule out bacterial infection given the fever and sore throat.

Patient presents for diabetes follow-up with active Type 2 diabetes mellitus and essential hypertension. Recent HbA1c was 8.2% (high) from 2026-02-10, and blood pressure was 142/88 mmHg measured today. Patient is on Metformin and Amlodipine, with no known allergies.
Metformin, 500 mg, tablet, dose 1 tablet, Oral, twice daily; for diabetes; started 2017-06-01.
Amlodipine, 5 mg, tablet, dose 1 tablet, Oral, once daily; for blood pressure; started 2019-08-12.
Consider repeating HbA1c in three months.

Patient presents with chest pain since this morning, confirmed as pain in the centre of the chest spreading to the left arm. Blood pressure is 150/95 mmHg and heart rate is 104 bpm. Allergy status is not recorded.
Pain in the centre of the chest.
The pain spreads to the left arm.
Consider cardiac evaluation given chest pain spreading to the left arm and elevated heart rate.
The patient presents with fever for two days and eating less than usual. Temperature is 39.1 °C and heart rate is 128 bpm. Allergy status is not recorded.
Consider evaluating the cause of fever and reduced appetite in a child with a temperature of 39.1 °C and heart rate of 128 bpm.
May be worth considering a physical examination to assess the source of fever and reduced appetite.
Duration of fever beyond two days
Patient's specific health concerns or symptoms prompting the visit.
Patient's vital signs or physical examination findings.

The patient presents with headache and dizziness for a week, with headache mostly occurring in the morning. Blood pressure readings were 120/80 mmHg by staff and 160/100 mmHg by device today. There are no known allergies. Medical history and the duration of dizziness are not recorded.
Headache and dizziness for a week.
Blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, measured by staff, this visit.
Blood pressure 160/100 mmHg, device reading (accepted), this visit.
Consider the discrepancy between the staff-measured blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg and the device reading of 160/100 mmHg.
May be worth investigating causes of morning headaches.
Burning when passing urine for two days
Consider urinary tract infection given burning when passing urine.
May be worth checking for sulfonamide sensitivity given the recorded allergy to Sulfamethoxazole.

The patient presents with a ten-day cough that is dry and worse at night. Temperature was 36.9 °C on 2026-10-04. A moderate penicillin allergy with hives was recorded in 2025-01-20. An assessment of viral upper respiratory infection from 2026-03-14 is available.
Consider viral upper respiratory infection given the assessment from 2026-03-14.

The patient presents with wheeze for two weeks, worse at night, and requires a reliever inhaler most nights. She has a history of active asthma since 2010 and is currently on Salbutamol and Budesonide. Oxygen saturation was 96% and respiratory rate was 20 per minute at this visit.
Wheeze for two weeks, worse at night.
Needs the reliever inhaler most nights.
Salbutamol, 100 mcg, inhaler, dose 2 puffs, Inhaled, when needed; for wheeze; started 2010-05-05.
Budesonide, 200 mcg, inhaler, dose 1 puff, Inhaled, twice daily; for asthma; started 2023-02-01.
Consider whether the current asthma management is adequate given the recent worsening of symptoms.
May be worth reviewing the current asthma controller medication in light of the recent increase in reliever use.

The patient presents with dizziness and tiredness. Heart rate is 48 bpm and blood pressure is 108/66 mmHg. She has a history of essential hypertension and stopped Atenolol due to slow heart rate, currently taking Ramipril. Allergy status is no known allergies.
Stopped Atenolol, 50 mg, tablet, dose 1 tablet, Oral, once daily; for blood pressure; started 2021-03-10; stopped 2026-05-01 (slow heart rate)
Current medicine: Ramipril, 5 mg, capsule, dose 1 capsule, Oral, once daily; for blood pressure; started 2026-05-01
Ramipril, 5 mg, capsule, dose 1 capsule, Oral, once daily; for blood pressure; started 2026-05-01
Consider the association between the stopped Atenolol due to slow heart rate and the current heart rate of 48 bpm.
May be worth investigating the cause of dizziness and tiredness in the context of bradycardia.
Consider an ECG to evaluate the heart rate of 48 bpm.
Consider the history of stopping Atenolol due to slow heart rate when reviewing the current heart rate of 48 bpm.

Patient presents with cough and breathlessness on climbing stairs for a month. Known conditions include active COPD and controlled Type 2 diabetes. Oxygen saturation is 93 %. Current medications are Tiotropium and Metformin. HbA1c was 7.1 % in June 2026.
